biggest_gap.what: The regenerated RI-CMB07 exemplar is a 120-second, 7200-frame fight in which the player is never hit. Measured from the shipped statistics file and independently recomputed from the JSONL: swings taken 0 (band 0.05-0.35), damage taken / max HP 0 (band 0.4-1.6), player hp at fight end 620/620, frames at exactly 0 stamina 0 (band 20-600), mean stamina 0.8303 (band 0.55-0.80), 45.87% of frames above 90% stamina (band 0.12-0.45), whiff rate 0.72 (band 0.03-0.25), swings negated by i-frames 0.115 (band 0.4-0.8), longest committed run 155 f (band 180-520), punish-window usage rate null. Eleven of twenty-four banded rows are out of band against RI-CMB07 M2's floor of at most four, over one fight against a floor of five. Of the enemy's 26 swings, 11.5% were dodged and 7.7% blocked; the other 81% simply missed.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The exemplar is the artifact RI-CMB03 M7, RI-CMB05 §B, RI-CMB09 §3 and RI-AI03 all diff against, so a fight with no danger in it makes every one of those checks pass for the wrong reason and hides the real defects underneath - the guard-break window that regenerates stamina and the hitstun lengths that are six frames long, neither of which the exemplar could ever have exposed because the player is never guard-broken and never staggered in it.

remedy.action: Rewrite the exemplar bot in tools/harness/cmb-exemplar.mjs so it fights inside the enemy's reach band instead of drifting out of it: hold 1.2-2.2 m from the target during ATK_WINDUP rather than retreating, commit to a punish inside every declared recovery window, and take the trade when stamina is short instead of walking away. Add an explicit assertion pass that refuses to write the exemplar unless it clears RI-CMB07 M2, and generate five seeded fights and take the row-wise median as the item requires.
remedy.acceptance: Over the row-wise median of five seeded fights: at least 20 of the 24 banded rows inside band, with rows 13 (swings taken) in 0.05-0.35, 14 (damage taken / max HP) in 0.4-1.6, 16 (frames at exactly 0 stamina) in 20-600, 17 in 0.03-0.20, 18 in 0.12-0.45, 19 in 0.55-0.80 and 25 in 180-520 all inside band individually, row 27 (punish-window usage rate) a number in 0.50-0.95 rather than null, and at least one GUARD_BREAK and one stagger present in the trace so RI-CMB03 M5 and RI-CMB05 M3 have something to measure.

secondary_observations.what: GUARD_BREAK regenerates stamina at the full 0.75/frame from frame 43 of the break, though RI-CMB03 §A specifies a x0.00 guard-broken multiplier and §D specifies regen suspended for the whole duration with the delay re-armed at its end. Measured: entry f80 at 0.00 stamina, regen at f123/124/125 while still GUARD_BREAK, exit f126 at 2.25.

Every hitstun state is corpus_length + hitstop_frames long: GUARD_BREAK 46 f against 40, medium stagger 50 f against 44, heavy stagger 70 f against 64, with the attack declaring hitstop_frames 6. One cause, three symptoms.

Jump does not exist. The button is accepted, produces no state change, no vertical displacement over 90 frames and no stamina spend, against a declared cost of 18 in game/data/combat/stamina.json. two_hand, swap_right, swap_left and menu are likewise inert. This makes RI-CMB02 §C's jump-attack and two-handed rows and RI-CMB01 §B's OVERLOADED jump prohibition structurally unmeasurable.
A parry with the default medium shield costs 26 stamina, not the 22 flat RI-CMB03 §B specifies. The build ships an undeclared parry_medium_shield: 26 that no reference item authorises.

Measured peak blade-tip speed exceeds RI-CMB04 §B's declared column on all 14 rows, by x1.00 to x2.69 (halberd R1 59.1 m/s against a declared 22.0). A one-handed straight-sword R1 rotates the blade through 615 deg in total and through MORE arc during recovery (280 deg) than during the active window (156 deg); the halberd totals 665 deg. The weapon also snaps 1.42-2.54 m in a single frame at the boundary between the attack pose and idle. The frame data is right to the frame and the motion is a windmill, which is also why §C's substep derivation is invalid.

Thin-weapon tunnelling does NOT occur, and the reason is worth recording. Under the discrete-pose model RI-CMB04 §C's substep rationale assumes, a 0.06 m pole would be missed at 8-282 grid positions per class (halberd 282 of 18,965 continuous hits). The shipped build sweeps by convex hull instead: forcing substeps from 4 to 1 changed no outcome anywhere across 168 placements and two 0.15 m fine sweeps, and the sim hits five placements a two-pose test misses. Sweeping is real; the substep count is observationally decorative.

The harness is fail-closed and loud in exactly the way RI-MTH04 asks: queueEnemyScript with an undeclared move throws 'Refusing to silently do nothing on a scripted frame - that would be a fabricated measurement (RI-MTH04)'. The probe_pulse fixture's 8 m hitbox radius is declared in the data tree rather than special-cased in a tool.

AMENDMENT-W1-09-01 is EARNED. Independently reproduced at seed 1337 pressing roll every frame for 900 frames: rolls start at 2, 54, 106, 158, 210, 262, 314 (cadence a flat 52), the bar reads 21.75 after six rolls and 6.50 after seven, and the first input is dropped for insufficient stamina at frame 366 - seven rolls and 366 frames against RI-CMB09 §3's printed five and 260. Nine frames of each 52-frame cycle regenerate, giving 6.75 stamina, not the 0 the item prints. The amendment corrects a derived table against the item's own two constants, changes no binding number, and makes the item harder to satisfy.

AR-3: this piece is NOT seam-sterile. topicsKnown, faction rank, expulsion, rival standing, disposition and the gold purse - all set outside the fight - decide at 60 Hz whether a hostile ends the encounter alive, and the outcome writes back to faction standing and to whether a soul drops. Ten measured gate cases confirm the ladder, including a lore topic ending a fight at disposition 0 where gold and rank both fail.

corpus_extended.note: M2's step 3 infers 'sweeping is not implemented' from 'forcing substeps to 1 produces no misses'. That inference is valid only for a discrete-pose sweep. For a convex-hull sweep, reducing substeps WIDENS coverage in the concave interior of an arc and narrows it nowhere, so the tell can never fire however broken the build is - which is exactly what happened here (critic-geo2-substeps1.json is byte-for-byte equivalent in outcome to critic-geo2.json). Proposed replacement: a concave-interior phantom-coverage test (place the target inside the chord of the swing and require sim = analytic there), plus shipping the 0.06 m pole fixture M2 already names and which no build provides.

Both items' blind pairs compare our artifact against one generated from the item's own table. When the build is exact - which it is, bit-for-bit, in all four i-frame vectors and all 14 census rows - the two sides of the pack are identical and no discriminating question exists. A blind pair whose sides coincide when the work is correct cannot discriminate. It needs a property that varies WITHIN correctness: the shape of the roll's per-frame root-delta curve, or the buffered/ignored boundary of the commitment grid.

RI-CMB03 M5 says 'set stamina to dmg x (1-stability) - 1 and block'; RI-CMB04 M2 says 're-run with substeps forced to 1'; RI-CMB06 M4 asks for 8 camera yaws. None is reachable through window.__HARNESS. I obtained the first by sprinting the bar down for 600 frames and teleporting back to the enemy, the second by editing game/data/combat/hitgeometry.json and reverting it with git checkout, and the third only partially (the look channel is spring-damped and yielded 6 deg of camera travel). Three one-line hooks - setStamina(v), setSweepSubsteps(n), camera({yaw}) - would replace all of that fixture gymnastics.

arbitration_questions.question: Does hitstop count inside the hitstun state's declared duration, or outside it? Every hitstun length in this build measures corpus_length + hitstop_frames: GUARD_BREAK 46 against RI-CMB03 §D's 40, medium stagger 50 against RI-CMB05 §B's 44, heavy stagger 70 against 64. RI-CMB03 M5 and RI-CMB05 M3 both say 'exactly', and neither item says which side of the boundary hitstop sits on.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Souls freezes both actors for a few frames on impact and THEN plays the hitstun animation at its authored length, so the observable state is longer than the animation and the build is right; the corpus numbers are animation lengths, not state durations.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Not a Morrowind question. The competing reading is purely internal: RI-CMB03 §D and RI-CMB05 §B are written as state durations ('duration := 40 frames', 'stagger frames'), RI-WPN05 owns hitstop separately, and a punish window whose length depends on which weapon hit you is not a window a player can learn.

arbitration_questions.question: RI-CMB03 §A specifies a x0.00 regeneration multiplier while staggered or guard-broken and §D specifies the delay re-armed at the END of the break. The build regenerates at the full base rate from frame 43 of the break. Is the punish window meant to leave the player at zero, or merely to have started them at zero?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: The whole point of the guard break is that you cannot act AND cannot bank stamina for what follows; §D's 'regen suspended for the whole duration, delay re-armed at the end' is unambiguous and the build contradicts it.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: n/a - this is an internal contradiction between an implementation and an item, not a seam. Recorded here because RI-CMB03's own S22 note already flags §D as the one figure the rebase deliberately did not touch and recommends doubling it to 80 f@60, so §D is known to be unsettled and a builder could reasonably have read it as in flux.
